column1: # Every defect seen in a capture, and what happened to it.
# Tab-separated: id<TAB>plugin<TAB>lane<TAB>status<TAB>evidence<TAB>note
# status is one of:
#   open      seen and reproduced, not repaired -- defect_gate.py fails on this
#   fixed     repaired; evidence names the capture that shows it repaired
#   refuted   re-measured, the original report was wrong; note says how
#   accepted  the owner said in writing to ship it as it is
# Writing a row here is what makes an unrepaired defect fail a gate instead of
# sitting in a paragraph nobody re-reads.  Add the row when you SEE it, not
# when you get around to it.
LAYER-01
column6: WRONG as reported. The host re-resolves every subscription by name whenever the tree instance changes and raises UNBOUND; App_PluginLayoutTick passes instance 0 for the whole login screen, so a bound watch is back to PENDING before the poll would have spoken. What was missing was the test, and a testbed that retired a node identity on unbind instead of handing the same ref back

column1: LAYER-02
column6: REAL. PORCELAIN_INPUT_SCREEN was an enumerator nothing ever raised, so a description that watches no element (AT_CANVAS, a fixed corner) was never re-asked at a transition. Masked on the usual path because a logout unbinds every element. Porcelain now reads core.screen once per fence and stamps the input on a change
